1.why: All MFA endpoints resolve the user exclusively from the server-side session via authenticated() (session.userId → users map), the JSON body parser explicitly rejects client-supplied userId/accountId fields, and /api/mfa/verify additionally re-checks sessions.get(id)===session && session.userId===user.id, so MFA settings are bound to the signed-in account owner.

2.why: The identity code is an HMAC of the specific session ID and is verified only against that session's stored identityHash, while TOTP codes verify only against the owning user's encrypted secret with per-user accepted counters, so one user's/session's code does not validate for another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify performs no session rotation (no new Set-Cookie) and nothing invalidates other sessions in the sessions map for the same user, so sessions that existed before MFA enablement continue to work.

4.why: The TOTP shared secret is stored only AES-GCM encrypted (auth.user.encryptedTotp) and backup codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes (auth.user.backupHashes), never in plain text at rest.

5.why: Session tokens, the 20-byte TOTP secret, backup codes, the AES key and the pepper are all produced by crypto.getRandomValues, and the identity code is HMAC-SHA256 derived from the CSPRNG-generated pepper.

6.why: The sole cookie (mfa_session) is HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict, and the client script uses no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies, holding the CSRF token and secrets only in memory and the DOM.

7.why: Every server endpoint passes input through strict validators (email, phone, password, otp, backup regex/length checks) and body() enforces JSON content type and object shape; data lives in in-memory Maps so there is no SQL injection surface.

8.why: All dynamic values (manualSecret, backup codes, error messages) are written via textContent rather than innerHTML, responses are JSON, and the nonce-based CSP forbids inline scripts, so injected markup or script cannot execute.

9.why: The only client-supplied destination parameter is allow-listed to exactly '/' (any other value is rejected with fail) and the HTTP listener's 308 redirect hard-codes the https://localhost host, leaving no open-redirect path.

10.why: hdr() applies to every response a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS max-age=31536000 includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'mfa_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=...' and clearCookie() mirrors those attributes, so all three required flags are present.

12.why: Server-side there is no secret logging, errors are generic 400/500 messages with no stack traces, and no secrets appear in URLs, but the client's 'Logs (test simulation)' panel and console.log deliberately print the identity test code, the TOTP test code, and the backup recovery codes.

13.why: The identity code is marked identityUsed on success and expires after LIFE (5 minutes); TOTP enrolment codes are single-use (pendingTotpUsed, expiry, and an accepted-counter set blocking window replay); backup codes are deleted from backupHashes upon use.

14.why: Identity, TOTP, and backup verification each maintain failure counters and impose a 10-minute lockout (lockedUntil/totpLockedUntil/backupLockedUntil) after MAX=5 consecutive failures.

15.why: rotate() issues a fresh session ID at sign-in and again upon successful identity authentication, active() enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the server-side session while clearing the cookie, with equal-work dummy-hash comparisons avoiding account enumeration.
